newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco to sell Alloys unit to Blackstone.
newsitem.headline: Inco to sell Alloys unit to Blackstone.

text.p: Inco Ltd., a major mining and metals company, has a definitive agreement to sell its Inco Alloys International subsidiary to Haynes International Inc. for about $410 million, the companies said Wednesday.
Inco, based in Toronto, expects an after-tax gain of about $85 million on the sale, they said in a joint statement.
Blackstone Capital Partners II Merchant Banking Fund LP owns about 80 percent of Haynes, a producer of nickel and other alloys based in Kokomo, Ind.
The unit of Blackstone Group L.P., a private New York investment bank, said it plans to merge the operations of Inco Alloys and Haynes after the deal closes in the fall.

Inco Alloys manufactures nickel and other alloys that are used primarily in the aerospace, chemical processing, power generation, pollution control and oil and gas industries. Its main operations are in the United States and Britain, with joint ventures, distribution and other related businesses in Japan, Canada, France and other countries, Inco said.

Inco said it plans to use proceeds from the sale for general corporate purposes, including the repayment of debt and the repurchase of its common shares through open market purchases from time to time.
The purchase price is subject to adjustment based upon Inco Alloys' net worth at the time of closing. The deal is subject to regulatory and other approvals, including antitrust clearance.
